text:
anya: Quick sync — we need to standardize how SDKs map API errors -> exceptions, surface request IDs in logs/exceptions, and how streaming clients should resume after transient disconnects. I'm thinking a small design doc and a PR that implements it in python/node. Any gotchas?

sam: +1. core ideas: 4xx -> ClientError (no retry), 429 -> RateLimitError (retry-after), 5xx and connection errors -> TransientError (retryable). Always attach request_id from response header.

kai: For streaming (server-sent or chunked) there's also resume semantics. Node EventSource clients use lastEventId header; for our protocol we should include a resume_token in the stream payload so clients can reconnect from where they left off. If server sets `resume_token`, client should send `Last-Resume-Token: <token>` on reconnect.

leo: Agree on mapping. Small nuance: in Python we often want exceptions to be pickleable and include `.request_id` and `.status_code` attributes so infra+users can inspect them easily. Example Python exceptions:```python
class RedwoodError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, msg, *, request_id=None, status=None):
        super().__init__(msg)
        self.request_id = request_id
        self.status = status

class TransientError(RedwoodError):
    pass

class ClientError(RedwoodError):
    pass
```

sam: Node pattern: attach fields to the Error object and include `isRetryable` boolean. Example:```js
class RedwoodError extends Error {
  constructor(message, { requestId, status, isRetryable } = {}) {
    super(message)
    this.requestId = requestId
    this.status = status
    this.isRetryable = !!isRetryable
  }
}
```

anya: How should request_id be sourced? header name? we use `x-request-id` in most infra, but some services use `x-redwood-request-id`. Can we normalize so SDK looks for both?

kai: Yes - SDK should check response headers in this order: `x-request-id`, `x-redwood-request-id`, `request-id`. Normalize to `request_id` field on exceptions/log entries. Also when making requests, allow callers to pass `request_id` to correlate client traces.

leo: Debug logging: add `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` env var to surface raw http req/resp (with sensitive fields redacted). Log format suggestion: `ts level component message meta` where meta is JSON containing { request_id, route, status_code, latency_ms }. Keep logs single-line JSON for ingestion.

sam: Streaming disconnect behavior: when a stream disconnects, SDK should retry with exponential backoff up to N attempts, sending `Last-Resume-Token`. If server responds with 410 (gone) or gives no resume_token, fall back to starting fresh (and emit a `StreamReset` event).

anya: Tests + docs: we need unit tests that assert request_id is copied into exceptions and logged, plus integration test for resume flow (simulate disconnect + server returns resume_token). Who can own the PR?

sam: I'll start a PR for Python mapping + tests. Will add a mapping table and runtime flag to enable debug logs.

kai: I'll follow up with Node PR for the EventSource wrapper and header normalization.

leo: I'll draft a small doc page in the SDK section: `error-handling.md` with mapping table, examples, and logging requirements.

infra-bot: Note: observability pipeline already accepts `x-request-id`. If you emit JSON logs with `request_id` we can correlate automatically.

anya: Nice. Action items: sam -> python PR (tests + doc snippets), kai -> node PR (resume + header normalization), leo -> docs page. I'll open a short design doc and link in the PRs. Please ping me on the PR for review. :thumbsup:

sam: On it — opening draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/789 (draft).

kai: Added a small checklist comment to sam's PR about resume token header name and backoff params.

leo: I'll write the doc and put it under docs/sdk/error-handling.md, will link to both PRs when ready.

anya: Thanks all — that should get us consistent behavior across SDKs.
